[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
'''James Glasgow''' is estimated to have been born about 1830. His birth date and place have not been established.

James was a son of [[Glasgow-3474|John Glasgow]], the married farmer who died at Lisnagaver on 24 June 1885. The civil death registration identifies James Glasgow of Lisnagaver as the deceased man's son, present at the death and the informant.<ref name="FatherDeath">[https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/deaths_returns/deaths_1885/06280/4799372.pdf General Register Office of Ireland, civil death register], John Glasgow, Lisnagaver, 24 June 1885.</ref>

The record proves the father-son relationship but supplies no age, wife or other identifying details for James.

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-867]] is assessed at 91% (proved). The held 1885 Lisnagaver death return expressly calls informant James Glasgow the deceased John’s son. Current research records Glasgow-3474’s merge into Glasgow-867 and gives the death-to-867 identification as probable, so the direct parent clause is strong but the specific-profile bridge retains uncertainty.

Held citation and associated historical narrative address this selected father-child identity; no original was newly inspected.

Next useful test: Photograph the Rasharkin stone and reconcile the 1885 death with the 1851 census age.

Source basis already held: [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/deaths_returns/deaths_1885/06280/4799372.pdf https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/deaths_returns/deaths_1885/06280/4799372.pdf]; [https://geni.nidirect.gov.uk/search/death GRONI civil death index (https://geni.nidirect.gov.uk/search/death), John Glasgow, 24 June 1885, aged 78, Ballymoney registration district, D/1885/31/1005/7/2.]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.
